kinds: the kind → delete-path mapping. The KIND LIST is parsed from the
ElementType union in registryFile — never from this file; this file only maps
each kind to the file (and, inside the shared DeleteElementCommand, the branch
marker) that owns its delete. A kind may map to SEVERAL paths: each path is
assessed separately, because two producers where one purges and one does not
is exactly the divergence the gate exists to catch.
declaredFindings: pinned at the FIRST HONEST READING, 2026-08-12. Every entry
is named (kind/arm:path), never a bare count. An unledgered finding exits 3;
an entry no longer measured is STALE and exits 3 — debt that has been paid
leaves this file in the commit that pays it.
EXIT CONDITION (C71 §6): hard-0 across every kind, with the undo half proven
by executed read-back rather than by the presence of a restore call. When
declaredFindings reaches [], the gate is hard-0.

kinds.note: DeleteElementCommand's slab branch delegates to this command (C2 §SLAB-SYSTEM-AUDIT-2026).
No delete command exists: panels are REPLACED (ReplacePanelTypeCommand / ReplacePanelWithDoorCommand), never deleted. The mapping declares the absence rather than skipping the kind.
Slab openings. Wall openings are deleted as window/door and are covered by those rows.

declaredFindings.why: Undo re-authors sitsOn from the slab snapshot; edges authored by other commands (supports slab→wall, boundedBy) are not captured and are dropped by delete+undo.
One of two ceiling delete producers never purges — diverges from DeleteElementCommand's ceiling branch, which does. Two producers, two behaviours.
Branch purges all edges, undo re-registers the ceiling but restores no edges.
Same divergence as ceiling: the Remove* producer never purges while the DeleteElementCommand branch does.
Branch purges all edges, undo restores none.
Undo re-authors sitsOn only (§COLUMN-AUDIT-2026 §C2); supports edges to beams written by AssignBeamSupportsCommand are dropped by delete+undo.
§BEAM-AUDIT-2026-W7b re-authors sitsOn/supports from the beam's own snapshot — reconstruction, not the verbatim capture 3ee632f6 established for walls.
OI-036 added the purge; undo (OI-037) re-registers the element but restores no edges.
Registry kind with no delete command at all: panels are replaced (ReplacePanel*Command), never deleted. Declared absence, not an oversight — but the registry kind remains delete-uncovered.
Undo re-authors sitsOn for parent+children from the snapshot; contains edges (room→furniture, IFC-imported) would be dropped.
Branch purges all edges, undo restores none.

Slab-opening delete never purges. Today no writer emits edges for slab openings, so the strand set is empty in practice — but that is coincidence, not integrity, and F-INV-2 forbids counting it as such.
Grid delete never purges. No writer emits grid edges today; same coincidence-not-integrity reading as opening.

Levels are the TARGET of every sitsOn edge and both connectedByStair/connectedByLift endpoints. A purge-less level delete strands one edge per element that sat on the level — the largest strand-set in the estate.

Room delete purges boundedBy/adjacentTo/connectedTo/partOf and undo restores none of them — precisely the wall-shaped case where reconstruction is impossible (room edges are authored by detection commands).
